Simulate a complete creel survey dataset

Source: R/simulate-creel-data.R
simulate_creel_data.Rd

Generates realistic synthetic creel data using a five-level hierarchical generative model (day → trip → count → interview → catch). Caller supplies distributional parameters via params; no default data are bundled with the package.

The generative model follows Su & Clapp (2013) for the day and trip levels; the roving-clerk step follows Greene et al. (1995). Only the sampling step is taken from the latter: its own simulated anglers are deterministic – evenly spaced around the shoreline, all starting one hour into an eight-hour day, with trip lengths alternating between 3 and 6 hours – whereas the levels below draw from distributions.

  1. Day level: Every day of the season draws the number of angler trips from a Negative Binomial distribution; n_sampled_days of them are sampled. Unsampled days are simulated too, so the season's true totals are known.

  2. Trip level: Each trip draws its length (hr) from a Gamma distribution, capped at the fishing day's length \(T\), a start time uniform in \([0, T - L]\), and its party size from a Poisson (at least 1).

  3. Count level: On a sampled day, each count is taken at a uniformly random moment of the fishing day and is the number of anglers fishing then. Count times \(T\) is unbiased for the day's angler-hours (Hoenig et al. 1993).

  4. Interview level, set by interview_type: "access" – the clerk meets parties as they leave, every party with the same chance (70\ trip; "roving" – the clerk meets parties while they fish, each with a chance proportional to its trip length (0.25 times its length over the day's mean length, capped at 1, so slightly under a quarter of the day's parties), at a uniformly random point in the trip, and records the time fished so far (at least 0.1 h). This is the sampling difference Pollock et al. (1997) base the choice of catch-rate estimator on.

  5. Catch level: Catch accrues over the time fished. A party catches nothing with probability p_zero_catch; otherwise its whole-trip catch is Negative Binomial with mean catch_rate$mean * n_anglers * trip_length / (1 - p_zero_catch), so the population catch rate (total catch over total angler-hours) is exactly catch_rate$mean. Harvest is Binomial given catch. A roving interview's catch so far is the part of that trip's catch caught in the time fished so far (each fish with probability hours_fished / trip_length).

Because catch accrues, the ratio of means on access interviews and the (truncated) mean of ratios on roving interviews both target truth$catch_rate. Before tidycreel 9.0.0 each party drew one whole-trip catch regardless of time fished, so an incomplete trip carried the whole trip's catch over the hours fished so far and inflated any roving catch rate (GH #494).

Counts and interviews come from the same simulated trips, so the true effort, catch and harvest are known (GH #646): truth reports them over the sampled days and over the season. Before tidycreel 9.0.0 the counts were drawn independently of the trips and only the rates were known.

Usage

simulate_creel_data(
  params,
  season_days = 100L,
  n_sampled_days = 30L,
  day_types = NULL,
  species = "walleye",
  species_weights = NULL,
  interview_type = c("access", "roving"),
  p_complete = NULL,
  p_zero_catch = 0.4,
  n_anglers_per_day = NULL,
  start_date = Sys.Date(),
  n_counts_per_day = 3L,
  lat = NULL,
  daylight_hours = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

params

Named list of distributional parameters. Required. Must include named sub-lists: effort (with gamma_shape, gamma_rate for rgamma()); party (with mean party size for rpois()); catch_rate (with mean, the catch per angler-hour, and nb_size for rnbinom(), default 0.5 when NULL or NA); harvest (with mean_pct as a percentage, e.g. 35 for 35%, default 35 when NULL or NA); counts (with mean_total_anglers, used when n_anglers_per_day = NULL).

season_days

Integer. Total days in the season. Default 100.

n_sampled_days

Integer. Number of days actually surveyed. Must be <= season_days. Default 30.

day_types

Named numeric vector of stratum proportions, e.g. c(weekday = 5/7, weekend = 2/7). Names become the day_type values in the output. When the names are exactly weekday and weekend, each day's label comes from its date (Saturday and Sunday are weekends) and the proportions are ignored; any other names are assigned to days at random in the stated proportions. When NULL (default), uses a single stratum "all". Note: passing a character vector (e.g. c("weekday", "weekend")) will error — the vector must be numeric with named elements.

species

Character vector. Species names for the catch table. Default "walleye". Catch is split proportionally across species using species_weights.

species_weights

Numeric vector. Relative catch weight per species. Must be same length as species. Default equal weights.

interview_type

"access" (default) or "roving": how the clerk meets parties, and so whether trips are complete or incomplete. See Details. Simulate twice for a survey that collects both.

p_complete

Removed in tidycreel 9.0.0; supplying it is an error. interview_type now decides trip status. The old argument mixed complete and incomplete trips in one length-biased draw (GH #494).

p_zero_catch

Numeric in [0, 1). Probability a trip has zero total catch (zero-inflation). Default 0.40. Note: this cannot be derived from a survey inventory (API artifact); the default is an empirical estimate from the creel literature.

n_anglers_per_day

Numeric. Mean number of angler parties fishing on each day of the season (sampled or not). Overrides params$counts$mean_total_anglers when specified. Default NULL (use params).

start_date

Date. First day of the simulated season. Default Sys.Date().

n_counts_per_day

Integer. Number of instantaneous count observations per sampled day. Default 3.

lat

Numeric latitude in decimal degrees, positive north. The daily fishing period \(T\) is computed per date with day_length. Supply lat or daylight_hours, not both.

daylight_hours

Numeric. Length of the daily fishing period \(T\), in hours, used to convert instantaneous counts to angler-hours. Accepts a single value applied to every day, or a named length-12 vector of monthly values (names "1"…"12", or month.abb) which is matched on the month of each count date. Use this when \(T\) is set by regulation or field protocol rather than by daylight. Supply daylight_hours or lat, not both.

One of them is required: trips start within the fishing day and counts are taken at moments in it, so the day needs a length, and there is no honest default (GH #646).

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. Default NULL.

Value

A named list with four data frames and the true values:

schedule

Full-season calendar, one row per day. Columns: date, day_type, sampled (logical). Pass directly to creel_design as the calendar argument. Day types follow day_types as described there.

interviews

One row per intercepted angler party. Columns: date, day_type, interview_id, trip_status ("complete" for access, "incomplete" for roving), hours_fished and trip_duration (both the time fished at the interview, as a clerk records it), true_trip_length (the whole simulated trip; simulation truth no clerk observes on a roving interview – do not pass it to add_interviews), n_anglers, catch_total and catch_kept (both so far), species_sought.

counts

One row per instantaneous count. Columns: date, day_type, count_time (integer index 1…n_counts_per_day, in time order), total_anglers (anglers fishing at the moment of the count), daylight_hours (\(T\) for that day) and angler_hours (total_anglers * daylight_hours). Pass count_time_col = count_time to add_counts when n_counts_per_day > 1.

catch

Long-format catch table. Columns: interview_id, species, count, catch_type ("caught", "harvested", "released"). For each interview the rows of each type sum to its catch_total, catch_kept and catch_total - catch_kept.

truth

A list of the population values estimators should recover: catch_rate and harvest_rate (per angler-hour), and the realised effort_* (angler-hours), catch_* and harvest_* (fish) of every simulated trip, each over the _sampled_days and over the _season; and days, one row per season day with its parties, anglers, effort, catch and harvest.

The population of trips is simulated before anything about the survey, so a seed fixes the population: runs that differ only in interview_type, n_sampled_days or n_counts_per_day sample the same trips and report the same season truth.

Pass angler_hours, not total_anglers, to add_counts. An instantaneous count estimates the mean number of anglers present, not effort; effort is that count multiplied by the length of the period the count was randomised within (Hoenig et al. 1993). estimate_effort() expands whatever numeric column it is given and cannot tell the two apart, so handing it total_anglers yields a sum of head counts silently mislabelled as angler-hours. The counts table carries three numeric columns and add_counts will not guess between them: name the one you mean with add_counts(design, sim$counts, count_col = angler_hours), or pass count_col = total_anglers, period_length_col = daylight_hours.

When n_counts_per_day > 1 you must also drop the measures you are not using before attaching. total_anglers differs between the counts taken within one day, so aggregation has no single value to carry forward and would otherwise keep whichever came first. add_counts() aborts rather than do that (GH #162); select the columns you need, as the second example below does. daylight_hours is constant within a day and can stay.

Note that day_length gives astronomical daylight. Where the fishing day is fixed by regulation or access hours instead, pass that period as daylight_hours.

The schedule output can be passed directly to creel_design as the calendar argument. The interviews and counts outputs are then passed to add_interviews and add_counts.

References

Su, Z. & Clapp, D.F. (2013). Evaluation of sample design and estimation methods for Great Lakes angler surveys. Trans. Am. Fish. Soc. 142: 234–246. doi:10.1080/00028487.2012.728167

Greene, C.J., Hoenig, J.M., Barrowman, N.J. & Pollock, K.H. (1995). Programs to simulate catch rate estimation in a roving creel survey of anglers. DFO Atlantic Fisheries Research Document 95/99. Department of Fisheries and Oceans, St. John's, NL.

Pollock, K.H., Hoenig, J.M., Jones, C.M., Robson, D.S. & Greene, C.J. (1997). Catch rate estimation for roving and access point surveys. N. Am. J. Fish. Manage. 17: 11–19. doi:10.1577/1548-8675(1997)017<0011:CREFRA>2.3.CO;2

Petrere, M. Jr., Giacomini, H.C. & De Marco, P. Jr. (2010). Catch-per-unit-effort: which estimator is best? Braz. J. Biol. 70: 483–491. doi:10.1590/S1519-69842010005000010

See also

simulate_creel_catch

Other "Simulation": day_length(), simulate_creel_catch()

Examples

my_params <- list(
  effort         = list(gamma_shape = 2.0, gamma_rate = 0.8),
  party          = list(mean = 1.5),
  catch_rate     = list(mean = 0.25, nb_size = 0.5), # fish per angler-hour
  harvest        = list(mean_pct = 35),
  counts         = list(mean_total_anglers = 10)
)

# Basic simulation (single stratum)
set.seed(42)
sim <- simulate_creel_data(
  params         = my_params,
  season_days    = 90,
  n_sampled_days = 20,
  species        = c("walleye", "northern_pike"),
  species_weights = c(0.6, 0.4),
  daylight_hours = 12
)
head(sim$schedule)
#>         date day_type sampled
#> 1 2026-11-25      all    TRUE
#> 2 2026-11-26      all    TRUE
#> 3 2026-11-27      all   FALSE
#> 4 2026-11-28      all   FALSE
#> 5 2026-11-29      all   FALSE
#> 6 2026-11-30      all   FALSE
head(sim$interviews)
#>         date day_type interview_id trip_status hours_fished trip_duration
#> 1 2026-11-25      all            3    complete        0.565         0.565
#> 2 2026-11-25      all            6    complete        1.716         1.716
#> 3 2026-11-25      all            7    complete        1.004         1.004
#> 4 2026-11-25      all           10    complete        6.238         6.238
#> 5 2026-11-25      all            1    complete        0.581         0.581
#> 6 2026-11-25      all            5    complete        0.352         0.352
#>   true_trip_length n_anglers catch_total catch_kept species_sought
#> 1            0.565         2           2          0  northern_pike
#> 2            1.716         2           8          1        walleye
#> 3            1.004         3           1          0  northern_pike
#> 4            6.238         1           1          1        walleye
#> 5            0.581         3           0          0        walleye
#> 6            0.352         2           0          0        walleye
head(sim$counts)
#>         date day_type count_time total_anglers daylight_hours angler_hours
#> 1 2026-11-25      all          1             1             12           12
#> 2 2026-11-25      all          2            10             12          120
#> 3 2026-11-25      all          3             0             12            0
#> 4 2026-11-26      all          1             4             12           48
#> 5 2026-11-26      all          2             4             12           48
#> 6 2026-11-26      all          3             0             12            0
head(sim$catch)
#>   interview_id species count catch_type
#> 1            3 walleye     2     caught
#> 2            3 walleye     0  harvested
#> 3            3 walleye     2   released
#> 4            6 walleye     6     caught
#> 5            6 walleye     1  harvested
#> 6            6 walleye     5   released
sim$truth$catch_rate
#> [1] 0.25
sim$truth$effort_season
#> [1] 3886.976

# Multi-stratum simulation with day_types (named numeric vector).
# `lat` derives the daily fishing period from day_length(), so T, and with
# it sim2$counts$daylight_hours, follows the season.
set.seed(1)
sim2 <- simulate_creel_data(
  params         = my_params,
  season_days    = 90,
  n_sampled_days = 20,
  day_types      = c(weekday = 5/7, weekend = 2/7),
  interview_type = "roving",
  lat            = 40.699
)

# Round-trip: simulate → creel_design → add_counts → add_interviews
# total_anglers is dropped: it varies between the counts taken within a day,
# so aggregation cannot carry it forward (see the note above).
counts2 <- sim2$counts[, c("date", "day_type", "count_time", "angler_hours")]

design <- creel_design(sim2$schedule, date = date, strata = day_type) |>
  add_counts(
    counts2,
    count_col = angler_hours, # a head count alone is not effort
    count_time_col = count_time
  ) |>
  add_interviews(
    sim2$interviews,
    catch          = "catch_total",
    effort         = "hours_fished",
    harvest        = "catch_kept",
    trip_status    = "trip_status",
    trip_duration  = "trip_duration",
    n_anglers      = "n_anglers",
    interview_type = "roving"
  )
#> ℹ 47 interviews have zero catch.
#>   Zero catch is usual; check it is not missing data recorded as 0.
#> ℹ Added 67 interviews: 0 complete (0%), 67 incomplete (100%)
